\nLa Vuelta passed here in 2001, on stage 11, a day marked by two emblematic figures of the race. In the 8th of his 17 consecutive participations, Iñigo Cuesta went first at the summit early in the stage. José Maria ‘El Chava’ Jimenez eventually flew to his 8th and penultimate La Vuelta stage win.
\nThe sequence with the ascents of Mont-Louis and then Font-Romeu was used in the first half of stage 15 of the Tour de France 2021, en route to Andorra la Vella. Sepp Kuss took what remains the USA’s last stage win in the Tour and Tadej Pogacar was leading the overall standings.
\nAt over 1,800 metres above sea level, Font-Romeu is home to France’s Centre national d’entraînement en altitude (national high-altitude training centre). It was created in the 1960s for French athletes to prepare for the Olympic Games in Mexico. Among the many champions who have used these infrastructures, France’s Sylvain Chavanel settled in Font-Romeu. \nLa Vuelta passed here in 2001, on stage 11, a day marked by two emblematic figures of the race. In the 8th of his 17 consecutive participations, Iñigo Cuesta went first at the summit early in the stage. José Maria ‘El Chava’ Jimenez eventually flew to his 8th and penultimate La Vuelta stage win.
\nThe sequence with the ascents of Mont-Louis and then Font-Romeu was used in the first half of stage 15 of the Tour de France 2021, en route to Andorra la Vella. Sepp Kuss took what remains the USA’s last stage win in the Tour and Tadej Pogacar was leading the overall standings.
\nAt over 1,800 metres above sea level, Font-Romeu is home to France’s Centre national d’entraînement en altitude (national high-altitude training centre). It was created in the 1960s for French athletes to prepare for the Olympic Games in Mexico. Among the many champions who have used these infrastructures, France’s Sylvain Chavanel settled in Font-Romeu. In the finale, the bunch exploded, Yves Lampaert attacked with 1 km to go, and the Belgian eventually took the stage and La Roja.

La Vuelta passed here in 2001, on stage 11, a day marked by two emblematic figures of the race. In the 8th of his 17 consecutive participations, Iñigo Cuesta went first at the summit early in the stage. José Maria ‘El Chava’ Jimenez eventually flew to his 8th and penultimate La Vuelta stage win.
The sequence with the ascents of Mont-Louis and then Font-Romeu was used in the first half of stage 15 of the Tour de France 2021, en route to Andorra la Vella. Sepp Kuss took what remains the USA’s last stage win in the Tour and Tadej Pogacar was leading the overall standings.
At over 1,800 metres above sea level, Font-Romeu is home to France’s Centre national d’entraînement en altitude (national high-altitude training centre). It was created in the 1960s for French athletes to prepare for the Olympic Games in Mexico. Among the many champions who have used these infrastructures, France’s Sylvain Chavanel settled in Font-Romeu. La Vuelta passed here in 2001, on stage 11, a day marked by two emblematic figures of the race. In the 8th of his 17 consecutive participations, Iñigo Cuesta went first at the summit early in the stage. José Maria ‘El Chava’ Jimenez eventually flew to his 8th and penultimate La Vuelta stage win.
The sequence with the ascents of Mont-Louis and then Font-Romeu was used in the first half of stage 15 of the Tour de France 2021, en route to Andorra la Vella. Sepp Kuss took what remains the USA’s last stage win in the Tour and Tadej Pogacar was leading the overall standings.
At over 1,800 metres above sea level, Font-Romeu is home to France’s Centre national d’entraînement en altitude (national high-altitude training centre). It was created in the 1960s for French athletes to prepare for the Olympic Games in Mexico. Among the many champions who have used these infrastructures, France’s Sylvain Chavanel settled in Font-Romeu. At over 1,800 metres above sea level, Font-Romeu is home to France’s Centre national d’entraînement en altitude (national high-altitude training centre). La Vuelta passed here in 2001, on stage 11, a day marked by two emblematic figures of the race. In the 8th of his 17 consecutive participations, Iñigo Cuesta went first at the summit early in the stage. José Maria ‘El Chava’ Jimenez eventually flew to his 8th and penultimate La Vuelta stage win.
The sequence with the ascents of Mont-Louis and then Font-Romeu was used in the first half of stage 15 of the Tour de France 2021, en route to Andorra la Vella. Sepp Kuss took what remains the USA’s last stage win in the Tour and Tadej Pogacar was leading the overall standings.
At over 1,800 metres above sea level, Font-Romeu is home to France’s Centre national d’entraînement en altitude (national high-altitude training centre). It was created in the 1960s for French athletes to prepare for the Olympic Games in Mexico. Among the many champions who have used these infrastructures, France’s Sylvain Chavanel settled in Font-Romeu. La Vuelta passed here in 2001, on stage 11, a day marked by two emblematic figures of the race. In the 8th of his 17 consecutive participations, Iñigo Cuesta went first at the summit early in the stage. José Maria ‘El Chava’ Jimenez eventually flew to his 8th and penultimate La Vuelta stage win.
The sequence with the ascents of Mont-Louis and then Font-Romeu was used in the first half of stage 15 of the Tour de France 2021, en route to Andorra la Vella. Sepp Kuss took what remains the USA’s last stage win in the Tour and Tadej Pogacar was leading the overall standings.
At over 1,800 metres above sea level, Font-Romeu is home to France’s Centre national d’entraînement en altitude (national high-altitude training centre). It was created in the 1960s for French athletes to prepare for the Olympic Games in Mexico. Among the many champions who have used these infrastructures, France’s Sylvain Chavanel settled in Font-Romeu. So far I’ve been enjoying it, trying to take in every moment and let’s see what can come now. [The team is looking for a new sponsor but] we don’t race different than the whole year. We try to show ourselves, we try to look for opportunities, to take them, and just give our best. That’s our mentality, always. [Today] as always we have to look for breakaways. I think it may be a bigger fight today with the possibility of crosswinds at the beginning of the stage. But I don’t think the breakaway will make it to the finish as there’s a pretty long climb with some headwind if I’m not wrong. This can favour the bunch.
